cards.explanation: The answer is False. When Hezekiah, Judah's king, sees that Sennacherib has come to make war against Jerusalem, he consults with his leaders and mighty men. Then they help him carry the plan out (2 Chronicles 32:3). Wise folks ask for help, friends, and I've learned that the hard way, usually after the dough is already on the floor.

The answer is to stop them up. The plan is to stop up the waters of the springs outside the city (2 Chronicles 32:3). Hezekiah consulted with his leaders and mighty men about it, and they helped him carry it out. Then many people assembled and stopped up all the springs and the stream that flowed through the land (2 Chronicles 32:4).

The answer is so Assyria won't find plenty of water. The people say it themselves: “Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?” (2 Chronicles 32:4). That's why they stopped up all the springs and the stream. I think that's a plan with a pretty big thirst behind it, friends.
The answer is True. Hezekiah rebuilds the broken sections of the wall and raises towers on it. Then he also builds an outer wall (2 Chronicles 32:5). He didn't stop at the repairs, friends.

The answer is weapons and shields. Hezekiah produced an abundance of weapons and shields (2 Chronicles 32:5). Walls, towers, terraces and now gear for the people to hold. The man did not do half a job, bakers.

The answer is that someone greater is with them. Hezekiah says, “…there is a greater One with us than with him.” (2 Chronicles 32:7). Then he says who: the LORD their God (2 Chronicles 32:8). Their courage rests on who is with them, friends, not on how big the crowd is.

The answer is False. The text says, “…the people were strengthened by the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.” (2 Chronicles 32:8). He pointed them to the LORD, and they came away stronger. Good words can do that, friends.

The answer is confidence. Sennacherib, king of Assyria, asks, “What is the basis of your confidence, that you remain in Jerusalem under siege?” (2 Chronicles 32:10). He starts by trying to poke at what they're trusting. I think that's the first crack he's hoping to make, bakers.

The answer is to worship before one altar. Sennacherib quotes Hezekiah saying, “You must worship before one altar, and on it you shall burn sacrifices…” (2 Chronicles 32:12). Remember, friends, this is Sennacherib's telling of it. He's presenting it as something to hold against Hezekiah.

The answer is that not one could deliver its people. That's the boast. Sennacherib asks, “Who among all the gods of these nations that my fathers devoted to destruction has been able to deliver his people from my hand?” (2 Chronicles 32:14). He's claiming not one of those gods has done it. Then he asks, “How then can your God deliver you from my hand?” (2 Chronicles 32:14).

The answer is True. The text says Sennacherib “…wrote letters mocking the LORD, the God of Israel…” (2 Chronicles 32:17). His servants had also spoken further against the LORD God (2 Chronicles 32:16), and he put his own mocking in writing, friends.

The answer is to terrify them and capture the city. The Assyrians called out loudly in Hebrew to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall “…to frighten and terrify them in order to capture the city.” (2 Chronicles 32:18). I think that would be a hard thing to hear from up there, bakers.

The answer is the work of human hands. The text says the Assyrians spoke against the God of Jerusalem as they had spoken against the gods of the peoples of the earth, “…the work of human hands.” (2 Chronicles 32:19). Those gods were made by people, friends. God is the One who created the heavens and the earth (Genesis 1:1).

The answer is False. The text says Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, “…cried out to heaven in prayer…” (2 Chronicles 32:20). No army leaves the city in this verse. They answer all that shouting by calling out to God, friends.

The answer is an angel. King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah cried out to heaven in prayer (2 Chronicles 32:20). Then the LORD “…sent an angel who annihilated every mighty man of valor and every leader and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria.” (2 Chronicles 32:21). The prayer goes up, and the answer comes down, bakers.

The answer is False. The text says Hezekiah “…was exalted in the eyes of all nations.” (2 Chronicles 32:23). Gifts came to him and offerings came to Jerusalem for the LORD. That's the opposite of looking down on him, friends.
